topic: Voice cloning is a licence problem, not a technology problem
angle: The models all work; most of them cannot legally be used commercially
hook: Voice cloning works. The licence is the problem
caption:
Cloning a voice from ten seconds of audio is solved. What is not obvious is that the best-known open models carry non-commercial licences, and that restriction follows the weights wherever you run them. Free GPU does not change it.

slides.text: Voice cloning works. The *licence* is the problem
slides.subline: Most popular models forbid commercial use

slides.text: Everyone tests these on quality. Almost nobody checks whether they are allowed to ship the output.

slides.title: Licences follow the weights
slides.body: Running a non-commercial model on rented hardware does not make it commercial. The restriction is attached to the file, not the machine.

slides.title: Check the model card, not a blog
slides.body: Fish Speech ships Apache code with non-commercial weights, and the licence has changed between versions. Read the LICENSE on the specific repo you are downloading.

slides.caption: of clean reference audio is all a modern cloner needs

slides.text: You won't see this anywhere else
